chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no illness but it hastens to the body, waiting to see when it is ordered to take it, and in another narration: 'Except for fever, for it comes with a coming.'
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of diseases and fever according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical nature of illness, portraying diseases as active entities awaiting divine permission to manifest, which underscores the Shia concept of *tawhid al-af'al* (Oneness of Action) in pathology. The exception of fever (*al-humma*) highlights its unique, self-regulating nature compared to other ailments that require specific divine decree to take hold. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the interplay between spiritual causality and physical symptoms in Shia medical theology.

en.hubeali: H 14501 – From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Ayyub, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws said:

‘There is none from the illnesses, but it waits, prior to rushing to the body (infecting), until after getting orders to act upon it’. And in another report: ‘Except for the fever, for it starts working as it comes’.
en.sarwar: 53. From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Ayyub, who has said: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said:

‘There is none from the illnesses, but it waits, prior to rushing to the body (infecting), until after getting orders to act upon it’. And in another report: ‘Except for the fever, for it starts working as it comes’.
